notes.2: Makes about 40. Bake them on two sheet pans, swapping the racks halfway.

move.title: Pour it hot, beat it smooth
move.body: Pão de queijo is Brazil's cheese bread: little puffy rolls, crisp outside and chewy inside, made with tapioca flour instead of wheat. Today you'll boil milk and oil and pour it over the tapioca flour to scald it, beat in an egg and grated cheese, and bake spoonfuls until they puff.

why.title: Why scald the flour
why.body: Tapioca flour is pure starch. Hot liquid makes the starch swell and turn into a sticky, stretchy paste. That paste is what traps steam in the oven and gives the rolls their chewy middle.

why.title: Cool before the egg
why.body: The scalded dough is hot enough to cook an egg. Ten minutes of cooling lets the egg mix in smooth, and it puffs the rolls in the oven instead.

why.title: Oiled hands
why.body: The dough is soft and sticky. A little oil on your hands or the spoon lets each ball slide off round.

why.title: No wheat at all
why.body: Tapioca flour comes from the cassava root. There's no wheat in these rolls, so they're naturally free of gluten.

wrong.fix: The liquid wasn't boiling when you poured it. Stir in tapioca flour a tablespoon at a time until it holds a shape.

wrong.sign: There are bits of cooked egg
wrong.fix: The dough was still too hot. Let it cool 10 minutes next time before the egg goes in.
The dough was too warm or wet. Chill it 15 minutes and add a spoonful of tapioca flour.
Bake 5 more minutes, until they're puffed with light golden spots.

quiz.q: Why pour boiling milk over the tapioca flour?
choices: The hot liquid turns the starch into a stretchy paste
quiz.explain: That paste gives the rolls their chewy middle.

quiz.q: Why does the dough cool before the egg goes in?
choices: So the egg doesn't cook in the hot dough
quiz.explain: The egg should puff the rolls in the oven.

quiz.q: What flour is in pão de queijo?
quiz.explain: So the rolls have no gluten.

ingredients.text: a little more, for your hands

steps.text: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 400°F. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
Put the tapioca flour in the large bowl.
Put the milk, water, ¼ cup of oil, and salt in the saucepan. Bring it to a boil over medium heat, watching closely.
steps.tip: Milk boils over fast. Stay right beside it.

steps.text: Turn off the heat. Pour the hot liquid over the tapioca flour and stir hard with the wooden spoon until it's a smooth, sticky paste.
steps.look: Sticky, glossy, and lumpy at first, then smooth.

steps.text: Let the dough cool until it's warm, not hot.
Beat the egg in the small bowl with the fork. Add it to the dough and stir hard until it's mixed in.
steps.look: It looks slippery at first, then comes back together.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Stir in the parmesan until it's spread all through the dough.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg.

steps.text: Rub a little oil on your hands. Roll tablespoon-sized pieces of dough into balls and set them on the pan, 1 inch apart.
Bake until the rolls are puffed and have light golden spots.
steps.look: Puffed, with light golden spots, and they feel light.

steps.text: With oven mitts, take out the pan. Break one roll open. It should be hollow and chewy inside, not wet. If it's wet, bake 3 more minutes.

target.look: Puffed and golden, hollow and chewy inside

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Let the rolls cool on the rack for a few minutes, and eat them warm.

notes.1: Makes 12 rolls in a muffin tin.

vegetable-oil#2.text: a little more, for the tin

oven.text: Heat the oven to 400°F. Brush the 12 muffin cups with oil.
oven.look: Every cup is shiny with oil.

egg.text: Crack the egg into the blender.
egg.tip: Crack it on the counter, not the edge, so no shell falls in.

wash-egg.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.

flour.text: Spoon the tapioca flour into the cup and scrape it flat. Add 1½ cups, then the parmesan.

bake.text: Bake until the rolls are puffed and golden on top.

check.text: With an adult and oven mitts, take out the tin. Break one roll open.

target.look: Hollow and chewy inside, not wet

cool.text: Turn off the oven. Cool 5 minutes, then run the butter knife around each roll and lift it out.
cool.tip: Eat them warm. They get chewier as they cool.

add.text: Add the milk, the ⅓ cup of oil, and the salt.
add.tip: Liquids go in first so the blade spins easily.

add.text: Put the lid on tight. Blend until smooth.
add.look: Smooth and runny, like pancake batter.

add.text: Unplug the blender. Scrape the sides with the spatula, then blend 5 more seconds.
add.tip: Never put a spatula in while the blender is plugged in.

add.text: Pour the batter into the 12 cups, about two-thirds full.
add.look: All the cups about the same.

move.title: Blend, pour, puff
move.body: Pão de queijo is Brazil's cheese bread: crisp outside and chewy inside, made with tapioca flour instead of wheat. Many Brazilian families make it the quick way, in a blender. Today you'll blend a batter, pour it into a muffin tin, and watch it puff up in the oven.

wrong.fix: Scrape the sides with the spatula and blend 10 more seconds.

wrong.sign: The rolls spilled over the cups
wrong.fix: Fill them only two-thirds full next time.
Bake 5 more minutes, until puffed and golden.
They came out too soon. Wait until the tops are golden all over.

quiz.q: Why can you mix pão de queijo in a blender?
choices: Tapioca flour has no gluten to get tough
quiz.explain: Wheat batter gets tough when blended.

quiz.q: How full do you fill each cup?

choices: Steam, held in by the egg and tapioca

add.title: Why a blender is fine
add.body: Wheat batters get tough when you mix them a lot. Tapioca flour has no gluten, so blending it smooth can't make it tough.

add.title: Why they puff
add.body: In the hot oven, the water in the batter turns to steam. The egg and the stretchy tapioca hold the steam in, so the rolls puff up and stay hollow and chewy inside.

add.title: Two-thirds full
add.body: The batter puffs a lot. Cups filled to the top spill over; cups two-thirds full puff into round domes.
